text.p: Caspian Securities said Monday it reiterated its buy ratings on Brazilian federal telecoms holding Telebras and unit Telemig after the government last week sold two B Band cellular concessions.
-- Caspian also said in a report that it maintained its market-performer ratings on Telebras units Telesp and Telerj, serving Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro states respectively.
-- It said B Band bidding results on Friday "were within our expectations and do not change our view on Telebras or any of its operating companies."

-- A group including Sweden's Telia won bidding on the Sao Paulo state area concession with an offer of 1.326 billion reais, while a consortium, including BellSouth Corp paid 555.6 million reais for an area covering six northeastern states.
-- Because it was initially disqualified, Tess' winning bid hinges on a court ruling.

-- If another group, Avantel, were eventually declared winner of the Sao Paulo state area its cellular rates would hurt be below estimates of a 15-18 percent annual drop across the Telebras system, Caspian said.
-- On Friday, Telesp announced a cellular plan with monthly subscription rates of only 18.66 reais and lower usage rates at night to address competition, it said.
-- "We expect similar plans to be offered in the future," it said.

-- Telebras preferred was off 0.87 percent at 148.40 reais, Telesp preferred was flat at 344 reais, Telerj preferred was up 0.61 percent at 164 reais and Telemig common was flat at 173.50 reais at 1330 local/1230 edt in Sao Paulo.
